_proposal.status: DRAFT — not ground truth. Scoring ruled on 2026-08-15 (see scoring_ruling); the questions themselves still require an SME-seat ruling before merge (CLAUDE.md role gates; ADR-0005).
_proposal.target: evals/golden_questions.json — MERGE these ten alongside the existing q01-q10, which are NOT modified by this proposal. Result: a twenty-question golden set.
_proposal.why: The set is ten questions, so one question is worth 10 points and SPEC/03's '>=80%' bar is 'miss no more than two'. Coverage is also lopsided: ONE timeline question (q08) for a product whose entire thesis is date semantics, and zero questions touching the administrative stay that ADR-0007 was written for. These ten close that.
_proposal.corpus: Authored against four FR documents + three CFR sections: 2024-29957 (89 FR 106064), 2025-03118 (90 FR 10592), 2025-00830 (90 FR 4628) per config.BACKFILL_FR_DOCS; 2026-15920 (91 FR 50475) via the daily poller (ADR-0007). CFR: 21 CFR 101.65, 101.13, 74.303 per config.TRACKED_CFR_SECTIONS. The live corpus is now 49 FR documents / 1148 chunks; see corpus_premise_rechecked for what that changed (nothing that withdraws a question) and what it confirmed.
_proposal.corpus_premise_rechecked: 2026-08-15, re-checked at M03 close against the LIVE corpus (49 FR documents, 1148 chunks) rather than the 4 documents this draft was authored against. All three owed checks are now discharged and NONE of the ten questions is withdrawn. (1) q14 HOLDS, and on better evidence than it was drafted with: it was grounded only in tests/fixtures/ecfr_21_101.65.xml and its note said to withdraw rather than adjust it if the live index disagreed. The index carries 16 chunks for 21 CFR 101.13 including a dedicated citation_path '21 CFR 101.13(h)' (cfr-21-101.13@2025-04-28#0004), and chunk 2024-29957#0384 carries the regtext verbatim: 'The claim is made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in 101.13, with the exception of 101.13(h) when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section.' Both halves of the question are citable from the live index. (2) q16 HOLDS, with a caveat worth recording so the next reader does not repeat the alarm. 'front-of-package' now appears in the corpus — in exactly ONE chunk, 2024-29957#0367, as comment-and-response discussion inside the healthy rule about the relationship between the healthy symbol and FOP development. It establishes no requirement and no date, and the FOP proposed rule itself (90 FR 5426) returns ZERO chunks. So 'I cannot confirm that from my sources' remains the correct answer and the question still measures what it says. (3) The distractor pressure did go up roughly twelvefold, and it did NOT break retrieval: M02's probe set was re-run at 49 documents and still scores 9/9 with recall@8 = 1.0 (ADR-0011, evals/history/0e69ef1-retrieval-s3vectors.json). A failure of one of these questions can therefore no longer be attributed to corpus growth without evidence. STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: '$10 million' and 'annual food sales' remain at ZERO hits, so the q07 ruling holds at the current corpus. What this draft still needs is an SME-seat ruling, which is a human decision and not a verification.
_proposal.scorer_notes: run_evals.py check() is substring-only, case-insensitive, over answer_rows + answer + citations flattened together. Consequences honoured throughout this draft: (1) it cannot express 'asserts X' vs 'mentions X', so every must_not_contain here is assertion-shaped, never a token ban — the q07 defect; (2) must_cite_any is an OR and also falls back to the full answer text, so where a question genuinely requires TWO documents the citation is pinned with must_contain / must_contain_any groups instead; (3) must_contain_any takes a LIST OF GROUPS and each group is checked independently (run_evals.py:86-89), so multiple groups are used rather than the must_contain_any_2 key that q05 uses — both work, one is less surprising. AMENDED 2026-08-15 by the scoring ruling. Two further consequences of substring scoring, both learned the hard way and both now load-bearing when writing a question: (4) AN ACCEPT TOKEN MUST NOT BE A SUBSTRING OF ITS OWN NEGATION. 'affected' is inside 'not affected'; 'stands' is inside 'misunderstands'. Prefer polarity-safe forms ('are affected', 'you are affected'). (5) A BAN MUST NOT BE REPRODUCIBLE BY A CORRECT REFUTATION. Any question whose stem contains a false premise will be answered by restating that premise in order to deny it, so bans on such questions must be bound to the direction of the assertion ('...to', '...by', 'so...', 'was...') rather than to the claim itself. Corollary worth stating because it is the cheaper fix: where a positive requirement already fails the wrong answer, DELETE the ban rather than repair it.
_proposal.verification_owed: DISCHARGED 2026-08-15 — see corpus_premise_rechecked. q14 was the one question grounded only in tests/fixtures/ecfr_21_101.65.xml rather than the live corpus, and its own note said to withdraw rather than adjust it if the index disagreed. The index agrees, on better evidence than the fixture gave: 16 chunks for 21 CFR 101.13 including a dedicated citation_path '21 CFR 101.13(h)' (cfr-21-101.13@2025-04-28#0004), and chunk 2024-29957#0384 carrying the carve-out regtext verbatim. Every other assertion in this draft was already sourced to a document, chunk, ADR or skill file in the repo. Nothing here was verified by asking a model. What is still owed is an SME-seat RULING, which is a human decision and cannot be discharged by measurement.
_proposal.scoring_ruling: 2026-08-15. Routed through the sme-eval-triage subagent per CLAUDE.md, then every finding was REPLAYED THROUGH run_evals.check() — the real scorer — rather than accepted on the subagent's reading. 13 of 14 hand-written specimens broke as predicted. ALL TEN questions needed token edits; NONE was withdrawn, and no question's subject, required dates or expected answer changed. Two failure shapes, one root cause. (A) BANS THAT A CORRECT REFUTATION REPRODUCES, causing false FAILS — q11, q12, q13, q19, q20. These questions hand the model a wrong claim to rebut, and rebutting it means restating it. Fixed by direction-binding each ban ('extended the deadline TO', 'SO there is no deadline', 'WAS published on') or by deleting bans already made redundant by a positive requirement. (B) ACCEPT TOKENS THAT MATCH THEIR OWN NEGATION OR ECHO THE STEM, causing false PASSES — q12, q14, q15, q16, q17, q18. Worst cases: q18's 'affected' is a substring of 'not affected' (the q02 defect verbatim, reintroduced three days after that ruling); q14 passed the exact negation of its own correct answer; q16 admitted a fabrication AND rejected the best grounded answer, in the question written to guard against that very defect. WHY THE DRAFTER'S DISCRIMINATION CHECK MISSED ALL OF IT, which matters more than the defects: the same seat wrote the questions and the wrong-answer specimens, and phrased the wrong answers the way its own bans anticipated. A discrimination test authored by whoever wrote the bans tests the bans against themselves and always passes. The harness is sound; the specimens were not adversarial. TWO TRIAGE RECOMMENDATIONS WERE NOT ADOPTED, both because they traded a false pass for a false fail: narrowing q14's second group to ['101.65'] and q15's groups to [['74.303'],['101.65']]. Reasons recorded in those questions' notes.

questions.question: A colleague says our Red No. 3 deadline moved because the order was suspended for about a year and a half. What date do we work to, and did the suspension change it?
questions.note: Tests the single most load-bearing stay semantic: 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) SUSPENDS, it does not toll. There is no day-for-day extension, so a ~17.5-month stay (2025-02-18 to 2026-08-05) left 2027-01-15 at 2027-01-15. Source: 2026-15920 / 91 FR 50475 lifts the stay and CONFIRMS both dates — recorded as scope=dates_confirmed, predicate CONFIRMS, never SUPERSEDES (ADR-0007; .claude/skills/regulatory-domain 'Administrative stays'). The bait is in the STEM and the premise is TRUE — the order really was suspended for about that long — so passing requires contradicting the inference, not the fact. Same construction as the corrected q07. TWO DOCUMENTS ARE REQUIRED, deliberately: the third must_contain_any group forces the LIFT document to be named in some form, because an answer that gets 2027-01-15 right without knowing a stay ever existed is right by luck, while must_cite_any separately requires the ORDER that actually sets the date. An answer citing only the lift notice fails, and should — CLAUDE.md requires a citation for each claim, and the deadline is not the lift notice's claim to make. DELIBERATELY NOT FORBIDDEN: 'tolled'. A correct answer may well say 'the stay did not toll the deadline', and banning the word would punish the right answer for its vocabulary — the exact defect the q07 ruling removed. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15 (sme-eval-triage, then replayed through run_evals.check()). Three defects, all in the tokens, none in the question. (1) FALSE FAIL, confirmed by replay: the ban 'extended the deadline' is reproduced by the most natural correct refutation, 'no document extended the deadline'. The stem hands the model a claim to rebut and rebutting it means restating it — the q08 defect. All bans are now direction-bound ('...to', '...by', 'moved to'), which a negated restatement does not reproduce. (2) The accept token 'stands' is a substring of 'misunderstands' and 'confirmed' was satisfiable by 'the notice confirmed the stay' — i.e. by a TOLLING answer. Both replaced with date-bound forms. (3) The group ['stay','suspend'] was a pure stem echo (the stem says 'suspended') and was deleted; the lift-document group already forces engagement with the stay, which was that group's stated job. Follow-on from the same replay: the no-change group also needed the NEGATED forms ('the deadline was not extended', 'no extension'), because on a question whose stem asserts movement the natural denial is a negation of the stem's verb, not the word 'unchanged'. Removing bare 'stands' and 'confirmed' would otherwise have failed it.

questions.question: In mid-2025 we were told the Red No. 3 removal was not final and might never take effect. Was that a fair reading then, and what is the position now?
questions.note: The point-in-time question the retrieval probe set explicitly REFUSED to assert. evals/retrieval_truth.json r05: 'the point-in-time reasoning (what was the deadline on 2025-06-01) is M03's, from the STAY_PERIOD interval, and is explicitly not asserted by this probe.' This is that question, and it is the reason ADR-0007 stored the stay as a first-class interval (pk=DOC#2025-00830, sk=STAY_PERIOD#2025-02-18) rather than an edge pair. The 2025 reading WAS fair at the time: during a 371(e)(2) stay the provision has no legal effect at all, and the outcome was pending final agency action. It is no longer fair, because the stay was lifted 2026-08-05 with dates confirmed. A correct answer therefore has to hold two time-indexed states at once, which is what distinguishes interval reasoning from retrieving the latest document. STRICTNESS FLAG FOR THE SME SEAT: requiring the exact string 'February 18, 2025' is the tightest assertion in this draft. It is deliberate — that value is stored as the STAY_PERIOD start and an answer that cannot produce it is not reading the graph — but it is also the first thing to relax (to a ['February 18, 2025','February 2025'] group) if it proves to fail answers that are substantively correct. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. THE QUESTION ASKED TWO THINGS AND SCORED ONE. It asks 'was that a fair reading THEN, and what is the position NOW', but every token tested only the now. Replay confirmed a wrong answer opening 'That was never a fair reading' scored PASS. A first accept group now scores the then-half, with tokens chosen so that none is a substring of its own negation ('was fair' is not inside 'was not fair'). SECOND DEFECT, FALSE FAIL: the ban 'never took effect' is exactly how a CORRECT answer describes the stay period — during a 371(e)(2) stay the provision has no legal effect — so the question punished the reasoning it exists to reward. Deleted, along with 'the order was withdrawn' and 'the removal was cancelled', which a correct answer reproduces in the negative ('the order was not withdrawn') and which were redundant anyway: any such answer already fails the lifted/in-force group.

questions.question: Which CFR provisions does the Red No. 3 order change, what does it do to each, and do they all change on the same day?
questions.note: Tests amendatory-instruction parsing end to end — the {action, target} extraction from src/ingestion/metadata.py surfaced as an answer. Source: chunk 2025-00830#0002, the amdpar chunk, quoted in evals/retrieval_truth.json r09 as carrying 'Remove 74.303' and 'Effective January 18, 2028 remove 74.1303'. Falsify by reading that chunk. This question is the COMPLEMENT of q02, not a duplicate: q02 forbids 'January 18, 2028 for food' and so tests avoiding the drug date, while this one REQUIRES both dates and tests knowing which provision each belongs to. Avoidance and discrimination are different skills and the set currently only measures the first. Substring safety checked: '74.303' is not a substring of '74.1303', so the two required needles are independent. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. FALSE FAIL, confirmed by replay on two counts at once. The ban 'same effective date' sits inside the correct answer 'they do not share the SAME EFFECTIVE DATE', and 'all on the same day' is the verbatim terse correct answer to the question's own third clause ('do they all change on the same day?' / 'Not all on the same day'). Both deleted as redundant rather than repaired: an answer that really does collapse the two provisions already fails must_contain on the missing January 18, 2028. The two surviving bans are date-bound assertions a refutation does not reproduce. Separately the discrimination group was too narrow — 'do not share the same' contains none of ['different','not the same','separate','later','two'] — so natural correct phrasings failed on the accept side too; broadened.

questions.question: Beyond the criteria in the 'healthy' rule itself, which other CFR section's general requirements must a 'healthy' claim satisfy, and is any part of that section carved out?
questions.note: The only genuine incorporation-by-reference test in the set — SPEC/03 gives crossref_agent the job of resolving 'as defined in §', and q03 (the sole crossref-tagged question) tests the opposite behaviour, declining to assert an UNsourced cross-agency obligation. Nothing currently tests resolving one that IS in the corpus. Source: 21 CFR 101.65(a)(2) — 'The claim is made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in § 101.13, with the exception of § 101.13(h) when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section'. Paragraph (d) is the 'healthy' paragraph, so the carve-out is exactly on the claim at issue. 101.13 is a tracked section (config.TRACKED_CFR_SECTIONS), so the target of the reference is in the corpus and citable. VERIFICATION OWED — the ONE assertion in this draft not confirmed against the live index: the quoted text was read from tests/fixtures/ecfr_21_101.65.xml, a repo fixture. Before merge, confirm against the live corpus that (a) a 21 CFR 101.13 chunk exists and (b) current 101.65(a)(2) still carries the (h) carve-out. If either fails, this question must be withdrawn rather than adjusted — the failure mode it would otherwise create is the q03 false pass. Deliberately does NOT require a '101.65(d)(2)' citation: evals/retrieval_truth.json r07 records that the chunker emits citation_path '21 CFR 101.65(d)' and '(d)(4)' and there is no '(d)(2)' chunk, so a question expecting it would fail on a chunk that does not exist. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. FALSE PASS — the most serious defect found in this draft, and the one the drafter's own discrimination check missed. Replayed through run_evals.check(): the answer 'all the general requirements of 101.13 apply, INCLUDING 101.13(h); nothing is carved out' — the exact negation of the correct answer — scored PASS. It satisfied must_contain via '101.13(h)', satisfied the except/carve group via the word 'carved', satisfied the second group by echoing 'healthy' from the stem, and tripped no ban, because the existing ban '101.13 applies in full' requires that literal section number and the sentence above never places it there. Fixed by banning the negation in the forms it actually takes ('including 101.13(h)', 'nothing is carved out'), and by DELETING the ['101.65','healthy'] group, which could be satisfied by echoing the stem and therefore measured nothing. NOT ADOPTED from the triage: narrowing that group to ['101.65'] instead of deleting it. A correct answer ('a healthy claim must also satisfy 21 CFR 101.13, except (h)') need never name 101.65 at all, so the narrowed group would have traded a false pass for a false fail. The token '101.65' is already reachable through must_cite_any. Deleting the group also removed 'no exception', which a correct answer reproduces as 'no exception other than 101.13(h)'. Also banned 'nothing is excluded' / 'is not excluded': 'excluded' is an accept token, so its negation would otherwise satisfy the group while asserting the opposite — the same shape as the 'carved' false pass, one synonym over.

questions.question: We make a strawberry-frosted granola bar that is labeled 'healthy' and coloured with FD&C Red No. 3. List every change we have to make and the date for each.
questions.note: The first question in the set that requires MORE THAN ONE verdict row. SPEC/03 defines verdict output as rows {product, trigger, required_change, real_deadline, confidence, citations[]}, and every existing question can be answered with one row — so the row structure itself has never been measured. One product here triggers two unrelated rules with two different deadlines, and the earlier one (2027-01-15, colour) is NOT the one attached to the more prominent claim (2028-02-25, 'healthy'), so collapsing to a single deadline is a plausible and wrong answer. Both dates are established elsewhere in the set, so this question adds no new ground truth — only the requirement that both survive in one answer. SCORER WORKAROUND, deliberate and worth knowing: the two FR citations are pinned in must_contain rather than must_cite_any, because must_cite_any is an OR and cannot express 'cites BOTH documents'. This works because check() flattens the citations array into the same searched text (run_evals.py:69-73). If the scorer ever gains a must_cite_all, move them. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. FALSE PASS, and the note as drafted overstated what a pass means. Replay confirmed that an answer with the two deadlines SWAPPED BETWEEN THE TWO RULES — colour by 2028-02-25, healthy by 2027-01-15 — scores PASS, because all four required strings are present and the bans only catch collapsing to one date. The two accept groups were both stem echoes ('Red No. 3', 'healthy' are in the question) and measured nothing either way. NOT ADOPTED from the triage: narrowing them to [['74.303'],['101.65']]. A correct answer may name the rules without their section numbers, so that fix trades a false pass for a false fail; the groups are kept as harmless. The swapped phrasings are now banned in the forms they most naturally take, but THIS IS A PARTIAL FIX AND IS RECORDED AS ONE: a substring scorer cannot express 'date X is attached to rule Y', so a swap phrased differently still passes. What this question reliably measures is that BOTH deadlines survive in one answer — the multi-row verdict structure, which is its stated purpose. Correct ATTRIBUTION is measured by q13 (74.303 vs 74.1303) and q17 (effective vs compliance), which is where that skill belongs.

questions.question: Do we have to put a nutrition summary on the front of our package, and by when?
questions.note: Honesty against a real, well-publicised FDA labeling initiative that is NOT in this corpus — front-of-package nutrition labeling, proposed at 90 FR 5426. That document is named in the q07 SME ruling as one of the rules the $10M tier actually belongs to, which confirms it is both real and absent here. Two ways to fail: invent a requirement, or answer from model priors about a proposed rule as though it were binding and retrieved. q09 tests the same instinct on an out-of-SCOPE product (dog treats, not human food); this tests it on an out-of-CORPUS rule for an in-scope product, which is the harder case because the honest answer is 'I have no source' rather than 'that is not covered by this rule'. DELIBERATELY NOT FORBIDDEN: the token '90 FR 5426'. Naming the initiative as something the answer cannot speak to is CORRECT behaviour; only asserting its requirements is wrong. This is the same distinction the q03 ruling drew for TTB, and it is the reason must_not_contain here is assertion-shaped. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. BROKEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — the q07 fourth defect, the one that is invisible to inspection, in the question written to guard against it. Replay: (a) FALSE PASS — the accept token 'do not have' is matched by the fabrication 'No, you DO NOT HAVE to add a front-of-package nutrition summary', which is an answer from model priors and precisely what this question exists to catch; (b) FALSE FAIL — the best corpus-grounded answer, 'my sources discuss front-of-package labeling only in passing and establish no requirement and no date', matched none of the eight accept tokens. The group is now SOURCE-SHAPED throughout: every token asserts something about the sources rather than about the world. Removed 'do not have', 'unable to' and 'outside' as matchable by unrelated prose. DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED: bare 'not required' or 'no requirement'. FOP is a real PROPOSED rule, so 'you are not required to' is true in the world and ungrounded in this corpus, and admitting it would readmit the exact answer the question is built to fail. That distinction is the whole content of this question. The 2026-08-15 recheck sharpened it rather than weakening it: 'front-of-package' now appears in ONE chunk (2024-29957#0367) as preamble discussion, so the ideal answer is no longer a flat 'I have no source' but 'mentioned in passing, establishes no requirement' — which the old token set would have failed.

questions.question: Give the publication, effective, and compliance dates for the 'healthy' rule, including any change made to them after publication.
questions.note: The 'healthy' counterpart to q08, which does this for Red No. 3. The two rules fail in OPPOSITE directions and that is why both are needed: the Red No. 3 order sets no compliance date at all (ADR-0006), while the 'healthy' rule sets all three AND has one of them moved by a second document. Sources: pub 2024-12-27 and compliance 2028-02-25 from 2024-29957 (chunk #0000, 'The compliance date of this final rule is February 25, 2028'); effective delayed to 2025-04-28 by 2025-03118 (chunk #0000, 'the effective date for the final rule published December 27, 2024 (89 FR 106064), is delayed until April 28, 2025'); 'the compliance date remains unchanged at this time' from chunk 2025-03118#0003. All four strings were verified by reading the chunks per evals/retrieval_truth.json r01/r06. This question is the assembly q01 tests obliquely: q01 asks the yes/no trap, this asks for all three dates correctly ATTRIBUTED, which is the failure mode ADR-0006 exists to prevent. The last two must_contain_any groups force BOTH documents to be named while allowing either the FR citation or the doc number, since the delay is unknowable from the final rule alone. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. FALSE PASS: replay confirmed that 'the compliance date DELAYED TO February 25, 2028' — the ADR-0006 conflation this question exists to catch, stated outright — evaded all four bans, because each required 'was', 'moved' or 'is' and this phrasing uses none of them. The ban list now covers the bare participle. Separately 'still' was dropped from the unchanged-group: it is satisfiable incidentally by any sentence containing the word, so it let a wrong answer clear the group it was supposed to gate.

questions.question: We sell a shelf-stable lentil soup labeled 'healthy'. Are we affected by the healthy-claim changes?
questions.note: The companion q10 has needed since it was written. q10 is the same question with NO profile and expects pending_review; this one supplies exactly the profile that matters and expects the gate NOT to fire. A HITL gate is only meaningful if it is measured in both directions — one that pauses on everything passes q10 perfectly and is useless, and nothing in the set currently catches that. The profile given is deliberately minimal: a product type and the fact that it bears a 'healthy' claim, no revenue figure, because applicability under this rule turns on CONDUCT (does the label bear the claim) and never on company size — 2024-29957#0303 Response 135, per the q07 ruling. If the gate demands a revenue figure before answering, it has learned the wrong applicability model and this question fails on status. LIMITATION, STATED NOT PAPERED OVER: this does NOT test resume, which SPEC/03's Done-when also requires ('ends pending_review, then resumes correctly'). run_evals.py only ever POSTs /query (run_evals.py:57-66) and has no way to POST /resume/{id}, so resume cannot be expressed as a golden question at all today. It needs either a runner change or a separate harness, and that is a SPEC/04 API-surface decision, not something to fake here with a question that appears to cover it. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. FALSE PASS, and it is the q02 defect verbatim, reintroduced in a question drafted three days after that ruling. The accept token 'affected' IS A SUBSTRING OF ITS OWN NEGATION: replay confirmed 'You are NOT AFFECTED by the healthy-claim changes; for those who are, the compliance date is February 25, 2028' scores PASS on every check. Every token in the group is now polarity-safe — 'are affected' is not inside 'are not affected', 'applies to you' is not inside 'does not apply to you'. SECOND FINDING: 'pending_review' in must_not_contain was INERT and has been removed. run_evals.flatten_answer() concatenates answer_rows, answer and citations only; status is never in the searched text, so that ban could not fire under any answer. The status assertion it was trying to make is already made properly by expect_status_any. THIRD, RECORDED AS A LIMITATION NOT A DEFECT: expect_status_any ['ok'] also fails when the confidence trigger fires, not only the profile-sufficiency one (src/graph/nodes.py hitl_reason: profile_sufficient first, then confidence < config.CONFIDENCE_HITL_THRESHOLD). So a status failure here means 'the gate fired', not necessarily 'the gate demanded a revenue figure'. Read `provenance` before calling it an applicability failure — otherwise this question can be mistaken for a reason to tune a threshold.

questions.question: Our supplier says the Red No. 3 order sets no compliance date, so there is no hard deadline for using up our coloured inventory. Are they right?
must_not_contain: so there is no hard deadline
you may continue using Red No. 3 after
they are correct that there is no hard deadline
your supplier is right that there is no hard deadline
questions.note: The hardest trap in this draft, because the premise is TRUE and only the conclusion is wrong. The order genuinely sets no compliance date — ADR-0006 and .claude/skills/regulatory-domain both say a repeal states only an effective date and compliance_date stays null, which is why a compliance-date range filter returns nothing for this document (probe r02). The operative deadline is DERIVED: after 2027-01-15 the listing is gone and the product is adulterated. Deriving and explaining that is named in the skill as the timeline agent's job, and the verdict must say which kind of date it is reasoning from. Nothing in the set tests it — q08 asks for the dates and accepts 'no compliance date' as an observation, but never makes the model act on it. CRITICAL AND EASY TO GET WRONG: 'they are right' is NOT in must_not_contain, and must not be added. The best possible answer opens by conceding the true half — 'they are right that the order sets no compliance date, but the effective date is the operative deadline' — and forbidding that phrase would punish precisely the answer this question is designed to reward. That is the q07 defect in a new costume. The forbidden strings are the false CONCLUSION only. SCORING RULING 2026-08-15. THE DRAFT GUARDED THE CONCESSION AND THEN BANNED THE REFUTATION. Keeping 'they are right' legal was correct and stays; the note's reasoning for it is upheld in full. But the concession and the correction arrive as a pair, and the correction restates the false half in the stem's own words: replay confirmed that 'they are right that the order sets no compliance date, but they are WRONG THAT THERE IS NO HARD DEADLINE' — the model answer this question was written to reward, quoted almost verbatim from its own note — scored FAIL on the ban 'no hard deadline'. The bans are now bound to the INFERENCE ('so there is...') or to an explicit endorsement, which a refutation does not reproduce. RESIDUAL RISK, STATED RATHER THAN ENGINEERED AWAY: an answer that quotes the supplier's full inference in order to reject it can still trip a ban. That is accepted because the real discriminator here is the positive side — the adulterated/unlawful/no-longer-listed group, which no answer agreeing with the supplier can satisfy — and further loosening the bans would buy little at the cost of admitting agreement.

questions.question: What date was the Red No. 3 revocation published in the Federal Register? Our compliance memo records it as January 15, 2025.
questions.note: Tests resistance to a wrong date the USER asserts — anchoring, not retrieval. Every other question in the set presents a neutral or self-serving premise; this one puts a specific false fact in the stem and rewards contradicting the person asking. Source: 90 FR 4628 published 2025-01-16. FDA ANNOUNCED the revocation on the 15th, and per .claude/skills/regulatory-domain the string 'January 15, 2025' appears nowhere in the document and must not be cited. Falsify by full-text searching the document for it. This is not a duplicate of q08 but its other half: q08 carries 'January 15, 2025' in must_not_contain and so tests not VOLUNTEERING the announcement date, while this tests not ACCEPTING it when handed over with apparent authority.
